A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, Table 1 and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical results and proofs, not original empirical outcomes. Symbolic-computation evidence is attributed to earlier work; Appendix A only links externally to numerical illustrations.

after.justification: V2 likewise reports theoretical results without original experiments, simulations or data analyses. The added appendices contain proofs, and Appendix B retains the external illustration link without reporting outcomes.

M1.justification: Gradient-flow training, ReLU path lifting and weight-product parameterizations are retained. The new prunability and strong-dynamics concepts are theoretical criteria, not changes to a training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical tasks. V2's additional analysis of graphs and initialization domains changes theoretical scope rather than evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Additional citations support mathematical arguments rather than introduce experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, metrics, budgets or testing protocols. The piecewise C2 losses introduced in Appendix I define a theoretical property, not an experimental setting.

E4.justification: The worked mathematical examples and perturbation analysis are retained. Added graph and reachability arguments are proofs, not new ablations, robustness evaluations or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. Table 1 retains the same theoretical summary; the new formal conclusions and proofs are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 3.2 and Appendix F's prunable-DAG and rank arguments, extending the Frobenius result to parameters with at most one zero under stated architectural conditions. Corollaries 3.3–3.4 specify initialization domains and establish conservation-law completeness that v1 explicitly left unproved. Theorem 3.9 and Appendix I also add a strong intrinsic dynamic property for piecewise C2 losses and a reachability argument extending the earlier metric impossibility result.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces v1's ReLU claim for any initialization with a claim for a dense set, and changes the linear necessity claim from intrinsic dynamics to the intrinsic metric property. These correct the scope of retained central claims; the overall research objective and principal contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 more explicitly positions intrinsic dynamics as a preliminary step toward mirror or warped-mirror implicit-bias analyses. It also adds discussion of dimensional restrictions motivating square weight matrices for nonzero relaxed balance. The open regime r > max(n,m) remains.

D1.justification: The same numerical-illustration repository is linked in v1 Appendix A and v2 Appendix B. No implementation, hardware, data-processing or experimental replication settings are added.

R1.justification: V2 adds Le and Jegelka on DAG conservation laws, Gleiss et al. on graph ranks, Isidori on involutivity, and Jurdjevic on controllability. These support the expanded theory without replacing the main research positioning. Gonon and Marcotte publication updates refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 revises the introductory motivation, moves recoverability into Section 2.4, and groups network applications under Section 3. It also copyedits retained prose and adds Appendix N's LLM-use disclosure. Much of the existing exposition and proof text remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The existing Table 1 moves from the main text to Appendix A without changing its entries. V2 adopts conference formatting, including running headers, revised headings and author-block layout; it does not add new figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: For this theoretical paper, Appendix F substantially strengthens the foundation by supplying rank and completeness arguments expressly absent from v1 and specifying admissible initialization domains. Appendix I further develops the linear impossibility analysis, while the abstract states the scope more accurately. Table 1 and the conclusion still retain overbroad universal initialization wording, but the added theoretical support provides a substantial overall improvement.
